title: PowerShell Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.question: Write-Output sends a value to the output stream. Here it appears in the terminal. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Write-Output sends one string to the output stream. The host displays it. Write-Output sends data; Write-Host is mainly for host display.

questions.question: PowerShell variable names start with a dollar sign. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The variable stores 3. Parentheses calculate 5 before it is sent as output. Use parentheses when passing a calculation as one argument.

questions.question: Double-quoted strings expand variables inside the text. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The double-quoted string inserts Ravi in place of $name. Single quotes keep the dollar text literal.

questions.question: -ge compares numbers using greater-than-or-equal. if chooses a block. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The -ge rule is true for 8, so the first string is output. PowerShell comparisons use names such as -eq and -ge.

questions.question: An array holds several values. Its first index is zero. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The array is zero-based. Its second position is index 1. Use @() when you need an array shape even with one item.

questions.question: foreach runs its block for each value in a group. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The range 1..3 supplies three values to the loop. The loop variable holds one item, not the whole group.

questions.question: A hashtable pairs keys with values. Brackets select a value by key. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The Title key selects Moon Trip from the hashtable. Separate hashtable entries with a semicolon or a new line.

questions.question: A custom object groups properties. Dot notation reads a property. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The custom object stores Pages as a property. Dot access reads 24. Object properties and a formatted display are not the same thing.

questions.question: Where-Object keeps values that pass a rule. $_ means the current pipeline item. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: $_ is each pipeline item. Only 8 and 9 pass the -ge 7 rule. Write the rule inside a script block with braces.

questions.question: ForEach-Object runs a block for each incoming value. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Each current item is multiplied by 2, producing 4 and 6. Use $_ for the current item inside the pipeline block.

questions.question: A function can declare inputs with param. An unassigned expression becomes output. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: param binds the supplied 4 to Number. The function outputs its product with 2. Extra expressions in a function can also become output.

questions.code: try { throw "Missing score" } catch { Write-Output "Try again" }
questions.question: try and catch handle a terminating error. throw creates one here. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: throw creates a terminating error. catch responds with the friendly text. Many command errors need -ErrorAction Stop to be caught by try/catch.
